slot.brief: Wire of given length, cross-sectional area (or radius) and Young's modulus under a known load; compute the elongation or the stress–strain pair, all from Y = (F/A)/(ΔL/L).

stem: A wire of length $2$ m and cross-sectional area $4\times10^{-6}$ m$^2$ is stretched by a load of $400$ N. If its Young's modulus is $2\times10^{11}$ Pa, what is its elongation?
working:
$Y=\dfrac{FL}{A\Delta L}\quad\Rightarrow\quad\Delta L=\dfrac{FL}{AY}$
$\Delta L=\dfrac{400\times2}{(4\times10^{-6})(2\times10^{11})}=1\times10^{-3}$ m

Independent check: Using ΔL = FL/(AY): (400 × 2)/(4×10⁻⁶ × 2×10¹¹) = 1×10⁻³ m.
solution:
Young’s modulus is $Y=\dfrac{FL}{A\Delta L}$, so
$$\Delta L=\dfrac{FL}{AY}=\dfrac{400\times2}{(4\times10^{-6})(2\times10^{11})}=1\times10^{-3}\text{ m}.$$
